title: Mediante: how the state built industry

sections.content: You know *mediante* ("by means of") from B1 Unit 24, a formal prepositional phrase of means. A noun follows it directly (not *mediante de*), and it often opens the sentence. Historians use it to say how governments built new industries: by means of tariffs, loans or state companies.

items.spanish: Mediante aranceles altos, los gobiernos hacían más caros los autos importados.
items.english: By means of high tariffs, governments made imported cars more expensive.

items.spanish: El Estado ayudaba a las fábricas mediante créditos.
items.english: The state helped the factories by means of loans.

items.spanish: Mediante estas ayudas, la industria creció.
items.english: By means of this help, industry grew.

items.spanish: Los gobiernos protegían la industria mediante impuestos a los productos extranjeros.
items.english: Governments protected industry by means of taxes on foreign products.

sections.content: Say how something is done with *mediante* + noun, then give the result: *Mediante créditos, las fábricas compraron máquinas nuevas*. Do not add *de* after it: *mediante créditos*, never *mediante de créditos*.
